title: The Black-Scholes implied volatility implementation in FE-R via the inverse Gaussian survival function
text: inverse Gaussian distribution, IG(μ,λ)\mathrm{IG}(\mu,\lambda), supported x>0x > 0 parametrized mean μ>0\mu > 0 shape parameter λ>0\lambda > 0. probability density function fIG(x;μ,λ)=λ2πx3exp⁡(−λ(x−μ)22μ2x),x>0, f_{\mathrm{IG}}(x;\mu,\lambda) = \sqrt{\frac{\lambda}{2\pi x^{3}}}\, \exp\!\left(-\frac{\lambda (x-\mu)^{2}}{2\mu^{2} x}\right), \qquad x > 0,  mean 𝔼[X]=μ\mathbb{E}[X] = \mu variance Var⁡(X)=μ3/λ\operatorname{Var}(X) = \mu^{3}/\lambda. cumulative distribution function admits closed form FIG(x;μ,λ)=N(λx(xμ−1))+e2λ/μN(−λx(xμ+1)), F_{\mathrm{IG}}(x;\mu,\lambda) = N\!\left(\sqrt{\tfrac{\lambda}{x}}\Bigl(\tfrac{x}{\mu}-1\Bigr)\right) + e^{2\lambda/\mu}\, N\!\left(-\sqrt{\tfrac{\lambda}{x}}\Bigl(\tfrac{x}{\mu}+1\Bigr)\right),  N(⋅)N(\cdot) standard normal CDF. survival function (complementary CDF) used therefore F‾IG(x;μ,λ)=1−FIG(x;μ,λ)=N(−λx(xμ−1))−e2λ/μN(−λx(xμ+1)). \bar F_{\mathrm{IG}}(x;\mu,\lambda) = 1 - F_{\mathrm{IG}}(x;\mu,\lambda) = N\!\left(-\sqrt{\tfrac{\lambda}{x}}\Bigl(\tfrac{x}{\mu}-1\Bigr)\right) - e^{2\lambda/\mu}\, N\!\left(-\sqrt{\tfrac{\lambda}{x}}\Bigl(\tfrac{x}{\mu}+1\Bigr)\right).  shape parameter λ\lambda follows convention Wikipedia article. statmod package (Giner Smyth 2016) instead uses dispersion ϕ=1/λ\phi = 1/\lambda, defaults 11, .e. ϕ=λ=1\phi = \lambda = 1.

what: The option time value as an inverse Gaussian survival function
title: The Black-Scholes implied volatility implementation in FE-R via the inverse Gaussian survival function
text: Let CC undiscounted option value, FF forward price, KK strike, TT time expiry, σ\sigma volatility. normalized time value c=C−(θ(F−K))+min⁡(F,K)=N(d1)−ekN(d2),d1,2=−ks±s2, c = \frac{C - (\theta(F-K))^+}{\min(F,K)} = N(d_1) - e^k\,N(d_2), \qquad d_{1,2} = -\frac{k}{s} \pm \frac{s}{2},  N(⋅)N(\cdot) standard normal CDF, θ=±1\theta=\pm 1 call put, respectively, ss kk total standard deviation absolute log-moneyness, s=σT,k=|log⁡(F/K)|≥0. s = \sigma\sqrt{T}, \qquad k = |\log(F/K)|\ge 0. key identity normalized time value survival function (complementary CDF) inverse Gaussian distribution, IG(2/k,1)\mathrm{IG}(2/k,\,1): c=ℙ(X>4s2)=F‾IG(x=4s2;μ,λ),X∼IG(μ=2k,λ=1). c = \mathbb{P}\left(X > \frac{4}{s^2}\right) = \bar F_{\mathrm{IG}}\left(x = \frac{4}{s^2};\,\mu,\lambda\right), \qquad X \sim \mathrm{IG}\!\left(\mu = \frac{2}{k},\; \lambda = 1\right).  Using closed form IG distribution λ=1\lambda = 1, μ=2/k\mu = 2/k, x=4/s2x = 4/s^2, survival function reduces F‾IG(x)=N(−ks+s2)−ekN(−ks−s2), \bar F_{\mathrm{IG}}(x) = N\!\left(- \frac{k}{s} + \frac{s}{2}\right) - e^{k}\,N\!\left(-\frac{k}{s} - \frac{s}{2}\right),  precisely normalized Black–Scholes time value cc. reciprocal 1/X1/X follows RIG law corresponds variable GG Madan, Roynette, M. Yor (2008); implied-volatility inversion needs IG side.

title: The Black-Scholes implied volatility implementation in FE-R via the inverse Gaussian survival function
text: representation makes inversion direct. Given observed price, form normalized time value cc, invert IG survival function, read volatility: x=F‾IG−1(c),σ=2xT. x = \bar F_{\mathrm{IG}}^{-1}(c), \qquad \sigma = \frac{2}{\sqrt{x\,T}} .  iterative root-finding: IG quantile function work. source code (R/blackscholes_impvol.R) maps line line onto formulas , cp playing role θ\theta: inverse Gaussian quantile F‾IG−1\bar F_{\mathrm{IG}}^{-1} supplied statmod::qinvgauss() (Giner Smyth 2016), called lower.tail = FALSE inverts survival function.
code: # normalized time value  c = (C - intrinsic) / min(F, K) timeval <- (price/df - pmax(cp*(forward-strike), 0))/pmin(forward, strike)  # IG mean  mu = 2 / k,  k = |log(F / K)| mu <- 2/abs(log(strike/forward))  # x = inverse of the IG survival function at c   (lower.tail = FALSE) x <- statmod::qinvgauss(timeval, mean=mu, lower.tail=F)  # sigma = 2 / sqrt(x * T) sig <- 2/sqrt(x*texp)
